key_insight: Parallel-SFT preserves universal coding skills during reinforcement learning by running supervised fine-tuning across multiple programming languages in parallel with RL updates, enabling strong zero-shot transfer to low-resource languages.
problem_solved: RL fine-tuning on a single high-resource programming language often overfits to language-specific patterns and degrades zero-shot performance on other languages; this work reduces the need to perform expensive per-language RL by improving cross-language transfer.
method: Parallel supervised fine-tuning (Parallel-SFT): maintain an ongoing SFT stream on diverse PLs concurrently with RL to anchor language-agnostic behaviors.
Mixed-language training/optimization: synchronize or mix gradients from multiple languages so RL updates on a source PL do not overwrite shared representations.
Regularization and anchoring: constrain RL updates (e.g., replay/parameter anchoring or output-level constraints) to preserve skills useful across languages.
impact: Makes code-focused RL more practical for many programming languages by improving zero-shot transfer, lowering compute and data requirements for low-resource PLs and enabling broader, cost-effective deployment of code models.
